svg.text: Self-hosted AI on Kubernetes, with A2A
The same cluster, but every agent is its own service: a concierge agent
specialist agents: one Deployment and Agent Card each
no GPU · each agent scales and ships on its own
traces, metrics, prompt versions, eval scores
autoscaling · GPU quotas · TLS · secrets · GitOps
Control plane (managed by EKS / AKS / GKE): API server · etcd · scheduler
The app reaches the cluster through the load balancer and the ingress proxy.
The ingress routes the call to the concierge agent.
The concierge asks the AI gateway for a model; every agent does the same.
mini is self-hosted: the gateway asks llm-d which pod, then calls that vLLM pod.
reasoning is a frontier model: the AI gateway calls the external API.
The concierge delegates over A2A; the AI gateway checks identity and limits.
The gateway forwards the task to the specialist's A2A endpoint, served by kagent.
The specialist calls its tools through the AI gateway: MCP pods, then the core.
Agents of other companies are reached the same way: A2A through the gateway.
Each agent keeps its own state in PostgreSQL; the OTel Collector traces every hop.
Without kagent the picture is the same: each agent serves its own A2A endpoint.
Steps 6-7 are a choice: agents of one team can also call each other directly, pod to pod.
Keep the gateway at the border, between teams and with other companies.
